units.title: Crack it: five ways with eggs

lessons.title: Boiled eggs
learn: Boiling an egg to the yolk you like
Peeling eggs without tearing the white

steps.text: Bring a pan of water to the boil
steps.detail: Use enough water to cover the eggs by about 2 cm.

steps.text: Lower the eggs in gently with a spoon
steps.detail: Turn the heat down to a steady boil so they don't knock against the pan.

timer.doneness: for a firm white and a just-set yolk

steps.tip: Like a fully hard yolk? Give them 11 minutes instead.

steps.text: Move the eggs straight into the cold water

timer.doneness: until they're cool enough to hold

steps.tip: The cold water stops the cooking and makes the shells easier to peel.

steps.text: Tap, roll and peel
steps.detail: Start at the wide end, where the air pocket is, and peel under a thin stream of water.

lessons.title: Scrambled eggs
learn: Low heat for soft, creamy curds
Taking the pan off before they look done

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt
steps.detail: Keep going until there are no streaks of white left.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low heat

timer.doneness: until the butter is foaming but not brown

steps.text: Pour in the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula
steps.detail: Push the eggs from the edges to the middle, folding as you go.

timer.doneness: for soft curds that still look a little wet

steps.tip: Eggs keep cooking off the heat. Take them off while they still look glossy.

steps.text: Season with pepper and serve on toast

lessons.title: Jammy eggs on toast
learn: Timing a soft yolk to the minute
Stopping the cook with cold water

steps.text: Bring a small pan of water to the boil
Lower the eggs into the boiling water with a spoon
steps.detail: Keep it at a steady boil, not a rolling one, so the shells don't crack against the pan.
steps.tip: Cold eggs crack in hot water. Lower them slowly and they'll stay whole.

steps.text: Cool the eggs in cold water

timer.doneness: until you can hold them comfortably

steps.text: Toast and butter the bread
steps.detail: Toast it until deep golden so it holds up under the yolk.

steps.text: Peel, halve and season
steps.detail: Lay the halves on the toast, then finish with salt and chilli flakes.

lessons.title: French omelette
learn: Keeping the eggs moving for small, soft curds
Rolling an omelette out of the pan

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the salt until smooth
steps.detail: Beat with a fork for a good 30 seconds, until the yolks and whites are one colour.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat
Add the eggs, then stir quickly while you shake the pan

timer.doneness: until mostly set but still soft on top

steps.tip: Keep the spatula moving. Small curds make a smooth omelette.

steps.text: Tilt the pan and roll the omelette onto a plate
steps.detail: Fold the near edge to the middle, then tip the pan so it rolls over onto the plate.

steps.text: Scatter over the chives and eat straight away

lessons.title: Shakshuka
learn: Poaching eggs right in the sauce

steps.text: Soften the onion and pepper in a little oil
steps.detail: Use a wide pan with a lid over medium heat.

timer.doneness: until soft and just starting to colour

steps.text: Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika
Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and simmer

timer.doneness: until the sauce is thick enough to hold a dip from a spoon

steps.text: Make four wells, crack in the eggs and cover the pan

timer.doneness: until the whites are set and the yolks still runny

steps.tip: Spoon a little sauce over the whites to help them cook evenly.

steps.text: Scatter over the parsley and serve with bread
